versions.changelog:
Compared with the previous version, this release includes:

- Clarified the core capability set so users can see more easily that `skill-enhance` supports not only skill creation, but also skill enhancement, local skill customization, and publish-readiness review.
- Improved the public-facing description and metadata so the skill is presented more clearly as a quality-first skill, not just a minimal draft generator.
- Reworked `README.md` so it reads more naturally as a GitHub project overview, focusing first on what the skill is, who it is for, how to use it, and what it produces.
- Strengthened the usage boundaries so users can more easily understand when `skill-enhance` is the right tool and when it is not.
- Improved the example prompts and explanatory wording so users can get started faster and better understand practical cases such as local skill optimization and release review.

Compared with the previous version, this release includes:

- Added a local-skill modification path so the skill can help improve locally available skills, including self-created skills, locally downloaded hub skills, skills stored by Codex or Claude Code, and `skill-enhance` itself.
- Added local-modification safety rules: the skill must first verify whether the current environment can access and edit the target path; if it cannot, it must say so clearly. If local editing is possible, it must confirm the target path and user intent before making changes.
- Expanded `SKILL.md` so local skill modification is now a first-class task mode across the workflow, output contract, and quality gates.
- Updated `README.md`, `agents/openai.yaml`, and example prompts so users can more easily discover that this skill can refine locally installed or downloaded skills.
- Extended `evals/evals.json` with local-path editing and editability-check scenarios to test the difference between analyzable, editable-after-confirmation, and not-editable cases.
- Extended the review references so release review now also covers local-modification safety, not only trigger quality, artifact completeness, and publish readiness.

This release includes:

- Added a new standalone `skill-enhance` skill that does not depend on the original `skill-creator` at runtime.
- Kept the valuable parts of the original skill-creation lifecycle while adding stronger quality and release-oriented review.
- Added five core quality gates:
  - Trigger Boundary Review
  - Output Contract Review
  - LLM Reliability Review
  - Artifact Completeness Check
  - Publish-Readiness Check
- Added stronger package expectations so a reusable skill is not treated as complete with only `SKILL.md`, but is reviewed together with `README.md`, `agents/openai.yaml`, `evals/evals.json`, and selected references.
- Added a first-class enhancement path for existing skills, not only greenfield skill creation.
- Added release eval prompts covering new skill creation, existing skill enhancement, trigger optimization, artifact completion, publish-readiness review, and non-trigger boundary cases.
- Passed structural validation and JSON validation for the bundled eval prompts, making the package ready for internal use and release review.
